problem: Pixel-aligned 3D reconstruction from unposed images struggles to recover complete scenes because it ties geometry to per-ray predictions, missing invisible regions and creating duplicated structures in overlapping views.
approach: NOVA3R learns a global, view-agnostic scene representation decoupled from pixel alignment using a scene-token mechanism that aggregates information across images and a diffusion-based decoder for complete point clouds.
contribution: Outperforms state-of-the-art methods in reconstruction accuracy and completeness by recovering both visible and invisible regions with physically plausible geometry.

problem: Extending reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards to real-world reasoning tasks is difficult because evaluation relies on nuanced multi-criteria judgments rather than binary correctness.
approach: RaR uses rubric-based feedback as reward signals for on-policy RL, aggregating multi-dimensional rubric judgments into structured rewards that guide model alignment.
contribution: Achieves up to 31% improvement on HealthBench and 7% on GPQA-Diamond over LLM-as-judge baselines by leveraging rubrics as reward signals.

problem: Cyclic learning—pairing inverse tasks with cycle-consistency—remains underexplored because current methods focus narrowly on domain-specific implementations without theoretical foundations.
approach: Formulates cycle-consistency as an evidence lower bound via variational inference, yielding two training strategies (single-step and alternating optimization) applicable across diverse tasks.
contribution: Establishes theoretical foundations for cyclic learning and demonstrates broad applicability via CycleGN (GAN-free alternative) and state-of-the-art performance on unsupervised tracking.

problem: Stereo disparity estimation via matching-centric paradigms is vulnerable to visual ambiguities from occlusion and non-Lambertian surfaces that local refinement cannot recover.
approach: DispViT shifts to a regression-centric paradigm using a single-stream Vision Transformer that directly regresses disparity from tokenized binocular representations, with shift-embedding to encode disparity shifts and a lightweight refinement module.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art accuracy with strong resilience to matching ambiguities and wide disparity ranges by prioritizing holistic regression over explicit matching.

problem: Existing red-teaming methods operate in text space and generate semantically similar prompts, failing to probe the broader spectrum of latent vulnerabilities in LLM safety alignment.
approach: STAR shifts exploration to the model's latent activation space via a strategy generation module that recombines existing strategies and a prompt generation module that translates abstract strategies into concrete jailbreaks.
contribution: Substantially outperforms baselines in attack success rate and strategy diversity, revealing critical vulnerabilities in current alignment techniques.

problem: Leveraging text-to-video models as implicit world models for viewpoint planning from 4D scenes requires adapting pre-trained T2V models to ground viewpoint predictions in 4D scene representations.
approach: AdaViewPlanner uses two-stage adaptation: an adaptive learning branch injects 4D scene representation into pre-trained T2V via conditional generation, and a camera extrinsic diffusion branch extracts viewpoints via hybrid-condition guided denoising.
contribution: Demonstrates superiority over existing competitors and proves the potential of video generation models toward 4D interaction in real-world settings.

problem: Anticipating generalization failures remains a central challenge because conventional mechanistic approaches provide little top-down guidance such as system-level measurements that predict and prevent failures.
approach: Uses task-relevant representational geometry to probe structure-function links and identify prognostic indicators of poor out-of-distribution generalization.
contribution: Shows that geometric properties of in-distribution manifolds (effective dimensionality and utility) consistently predict weaker OOD performance more reliably than in-distribution accuracy.

problem: Distributed self-supervised learning faces data heterogeneity challenges but lacks rigorous theoretical understanding of how D-SSL frameworks respond to non-IID data.
approach: Provides rigorous theoretical analysis comparing masked image modeling versus contrastive learning robustness under non-IID settings, introducing MAR loss with local-to-global alignment regularization.
contribution: Shows that masked image modeling is inherently more robust than contrastive learning to heterogeneous data and federated learning is no less robust than decentralized learning.

problem: Graph neural networks suffer from over-squashing, where information from large receptive fields collapses into fixed-sized vectors, creating information bottlenecks.
approach: Reframes over-squashing through storage capacity lens and adapts ideas from sequence modeling (associative memories, xLSTM) to develop a GNN architecture with improved capacity.
contribution: Demonstrates strong performance on capacity synthetic tasks and real-world graph benchmarks by increasing node representation storage capacity.

problem: Long reasoning in reasoning models requires efficient decoding but existing sparse attention approaches struggle to maintain accuracy while improving speed.
approach: SeerAttention-R learns attention sparsity via self-distilled gating and removes query pooling for auto-regressive decoding, trained on 0.4B tokens with 4K token budget.
contribution: Maintains near-lossless reasoning accuracy with up to 9x speedup over FlashAttention-3 on H100 at 90% sparsity.

problem: Attention sinks and compression valleys emerge in LLMs but have been studied in isolation, leaving their relationship and underlying causes unexplained.
approach: Traces both phenomena to massive activations in the residual stream via theoretical analysis and targeted ablation, proposing Mix-Compress-Refine theory of information flow.
contribution: Proves massive activations produce representational compression and establishes bounds on entropy reduction, unifying two previously disconnected phenomena.

problem: Unlocking advanced reasoning in LLM agents is hindered by scarcity of training data at the frontier of their capabilities.
approach: Introduces AgentFrontier Data Engine inspired by Zone of Proximal Development—an automated pipeline that synthesizes data at the intersection of independence and guidance, plus ZPD Exam for capability evaluation.
contribution: AgentFrontier-30B-A3B achieves state-of-the-art on Humanity's Last Exam, outperforming leading proprietary agents by leveraging ZPD-guided synthesis.

problem: Native Sparse Attention kernel implementation is inefficient for LLMs with smaller query heads in Grouped Query Attention, limiting applicability across popular models.
approach: FSA provides an alternative kernel implementation that enables efficient sparse attention across varied smaller GQA head configurations on modern GPUs.
contribution: Achieves up to 3.5x kernel-level latency reduction and up to 1.25x end-to-end training speedup on state-of-the-art LLMs.

problem: Teaching multimodal models visual chain-of-thought is difficult due to weak off-the-shelf visual CoT performance that hinders learning and lack of high-quality training data.
approach: Introduces Zebra-CoT, a large-scale interleaved text-image reasoning dataset (182,384 traces, 18 domains, 50+ tasks) covering scientific, visual, 3D, and logic reasoning.
contribution: Fine-tuning on Zebra-CoT yields +12% improvement in test-set accuracy and up to +13% gains on standard VLM benchmarks for native visual reasoning.

problem: Diffusion Policy has strong visuomotor modeling but high computational cost makes it impractical for real-time robotic control, and existing acceleration techniques don't generalize.
approach: BAC adaptively caches and reuses intermediate action features block-by-block, using an Adaptive Caching Scheduler for optimal update timesteps and Bubbling Union Algorithm to mitigate inter-block error propagation.
contribution: Achieves up to 3x inference speedup for free as a training-free plugin without modifying parameters.

problem: Long-context LLMs amplify distraction from irrelevant passages, degrading output quality despite larger context windows, and existing RAG and long-context strategies each have tradeoffs.
approach: LDAR learns to retrieve contexts that mitigate interference from distracting passages, balancing information coverage and distraction via adaptive retrieval.
contribution: Achieves higher performance with reduced token usage compared to long-context approaches across diverse LLM architectures and six knowledge-intensive benchmarks.

problem: Analyzing KL convergence for diffusion models under minimal assumptions shows dependence on data dimension and accuracy level, but existing bounds lack tightness.
approach: Uses refined analysis via Exponential Integrator discretization with ODE-based counterpart to stochastic localization, handling second-order spatial derivatives of score functions.
contribution: Proves convergence requiring O-tilde(d log^3/2(1/delta) / epsilon) steps with linear dependence on d, improving accuracy dependence while maintaining dimension scaling.

problem: Video scene segmentation relies on visual similarity between shots, missing semantic boundaries when transitions don't align with visual changes.
approach: Incorporates production-level metadata (genre conventions and shot duration patterns) into video scene segmentation via genre-based semantic pretraining and duration-aware anchor selection.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance on MovieNet-SSeg and BBC datasets with an extended MovieChat-SSeg benchmark covering movies, TV series, and documentaries.

problem: Multimodal LLMs integrate multiple vision encoders assuming diverse pretraining yields complementary signals, but this assumption often fails in practice.
approach: Systematically measures encoder utility via Conditional Utilization Rate (marginal contribution) and Information Gap (heterogeneity), masking encoders to quantify redundancy.
contribution: Shows strong specialization on some tasks (OCR/Chart >90% CUR) but high redundancy on general VQA, revealing that single/dual-encoder variants recover 90% of baseline performance.

problem: LLMs for formal theorem proving lack generalizability and are fragile to minor problem transformations, limiting practical applicability.
approach: Introduces EvolProver with data augmentation pipeline leveraging symmetry (syntactic via AST, semantic via domain translation) and difficulty (evolutionary instructions).
contribution: Achieves 53.8% pass@32 on FormalMATH-Lite and new SOTA on multiple benchmarks for non-reasoning 7B models via evolved training data.

problem: Earth observation foundation models are limited by training data scale, geographical coverage, and spectral diversity, constraining globally transferable representations.
approach: TerraFM leverages globally distributed Sentinel-1/2 imagery with modality-specific patch embeddings, adaptive cross-attention fusion, and dual-centering with class-frequency regularization.
contribution: Achieves strong generalization on classification and segmentation tasks, outperforming prior models on GEO-Bench and Copernicus-Bench.
theme: Foundation or frontier models, including LLMs

problem: Graph foundation models struggle with cross-domain alignment because they typically rely on modality-specific encoders that fail when graphs are pre-vectorized or raw data is inaccessible.
approach: MF-GIA captures domain characteristics via gradient fingerprints that parameterize lightweight transformations, using dual prompt-aware attention for few-shot learning.
contribution: Achieves superior few-shot performance across diverse graph domains and strong generalization to unseen domains without parameter updates.

problem: Scaling computer use agents requires large-scale human demonstrations, creating a critical bottleneck for developing human-like AI agents.
approach: PC Agent-E starts with 312 human trajectories and synthesizes diverse alternative actions using Claude 3.7 Sonnet to enrich training data.
contribution: Achieves 141% relative improvement over training on human trajectories alone and surpasses Claude 3.7 Sonnet by 10% on WindowsAgentArena-V2.

problem: Large language models increasingly curate bibliographies, raising the question of whether their reference lists are distinguishable from human-generated ones.
approach: Compares GPT-4o-generated references to ground truth via citation graph structure and content embeddings, using random forests and graph neural networks on paired graph datasets.
contribution: Structure alone barely separates GPT from ground truth (RF ~0.60) but embeddings achieve 93% test accuracy on GNN, revealing LLM bibliographies mimic topology but leave semantic fingerprints.

problem: Cross-modal matching tasks under small batches and scarce labels are limited by mini-batch subsampling and contrastive losses that assume all feature dimensions contribute equally.
approach: DART augments instance-level alignment with feature-level regularization via Unbalanced Wasserstein Distance, constructing reliability-weighted marginals that reweight channels by cross-modal consistency.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art audio-text retrieval performance with particularly strong gains under scarce labels and small batch sizes.

problem: Deep Q-learning couples representation and value learning, creating instability as representations must adapt to non-stationary targets while value estimates depend on shifting representations.
approach: SCORER models the coupling as a hierarchical game where the Q-function leads and commits to less frequent updates, while the encoder follows with frequent updates to minimize Bellman error variance.
contribution: Asymmetric bi-level optimization reduces bias and variance in value estimation across DQN variants with stable co-adaptation.

problem: Chain-of-thought reasoning in LLMs generates verbose thought processes with considerable redundancy, increasing inference costs and reducing efficiency.
approach: Uses step entropy to quantify informational contribution of reasoning steps, identifying and pruning redundant low-entropy steps via SKIP tokens trained with SFT and GRPO.
contribution: Shows 80% of low-entropy intermediate steps can be pruned without accuracy degradation, achieving significant efficiency gains on reasoning benchmarks.

problem: Video-to-audio generation must balance four perceptual dimensions (semantic, temporal, aesthetic, spatial) but existing methods conflate competing goals in single loss functions.
approach: PrismAudio decomposes reasoning into four specialized Chain-of-Thought modules paired with targeted rewards, using Fast-GRPO for computational efficiency.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art performance across all four perceptual dimensions on VGGSound and the new AudioCanvas benchmark.

problem: Art and design composition lacks interpretable, transferable structural priors that ground visual assessment and guide generation.
approach: Proposes compositional AND-OR templates encoding part-relation-geometry organization within a maximum-entropy log-linear model, learning via penalized EM with structured expansion.
contribution: Demonstrates strong agreement with expert paradigms and competitive performance with deep baselines while exhibiting higher human alignment.

problem: In-context learning and fine-tuning produce different generalization and inductive bias patterns, but the mechanistic origins remain poorly understood.
approach: Compares ICL and SFT as distinct learning algorithms by analyzing evolution of inductive biases and internal representations across model sizes.
contribution: Shows ICL preserves rich input representations but imposes stronger pretraining priors, while SFT suppresses task-irrelevant features, explaining weaker few-shot generalization.

problem: Large reasoning models suffer from overthinking on simple problems or underthinking despite capabilities, leading to inefficiency and potential inaccuracy.
approach: ReBalance uses confidence as a continuous indicator of reasoning dynamics, with steering vectors derived from hidden state prototypes to guide trajectories and modulate vector strength.
contribution: Reduces redundancy while improving accuracy across four models (0.5B-32B) and nine benchmarks without requiring training.

problem: Medical vision-language models constrained by text-only reasoning fail to ground inferences in visual evidence, limiting performance on fine-grained analysis and risking visual hallucination.
approach: MedVR uses reinforcement learning with entropy-guided visual regrounding and consensus-based credit assignment from rollout agreement for annotation-free visual reasoning.
contribution: Achieves state-of-the-art on medical VQA benchmarks by learning to reason directly with visual evidence without human annotations.

problem: Common practice initializes Transformer attention weights randomly or via simple alternatives, neglecting how initialization introduces optimization bias that shapes training dynamics.
approach: Proposes conditioned initialization that initializes attention weights to improve spectral properties, reducing condition number of attention Jacobian for more stable optimization.
contribution: Theoretically shows potential to reduce condition number and empirically demonstrates faster convergence and better generalization across diverse applications.

problem: Training specialized models for each visual generation/manipulation task is costly; existing unified approaches either require separate models or have limited task coverage.
approach: Many-for-Many unifies video/image generation and manipulation via lightweight adapters that unify task conditions, using joint image-video learning with depth maps.
contribution: Single models (8B/2B) perform 10+ distinct tasks with competitive performance versus open-source and commercial engines.

problem: Classical statistical theory for imbalanced classification is ineffective in high dimensions, leaving many overfitting phenomena unexplained.
approach: Develops high-dimensional statistical theory showing dimensionality induces truncation/skewing effects on logit distribution, characterized via variational problems.
contribution: Explains why minority class is more severely affected by overfitting and shows margin rebalancing mitigates accuracy drop.

problem: Minimizing inference cost via optimization (quantization, pruning) requires statistical tools to detect whether accuracy deviations indicate actual degradation or harmless noise.
approach: Proposes statistically sound hypothesis testing framework based on McNemar's test comparing model scores at sample level, with aggregation approaches across benchmarks.
contribution: Guarantees controlled false-positive rate and can confidently attribute accuracy degradations as small as 0.3% to actual model degradation.

problem: Direct Preference Optimization is sensitive to data noise and overlooks the differential importance of individual tokens for fine-grained semantic control.
approach: TI-DPO proposes hybrid weighting combining gradient attribution with Gaussian priors for token importance, plus triplet loss for structured preference guidance.
contribution: Achieves higher accuracy and stronger generative diversity with more stable and computationally efficient solutions compared to DPO.

problem: Model-brain alignment benchmarks rank models inconsistently across alignment measures, raising deeper questions about what constitutes true brain alignment.
approach: Introduces alignment patterns—characteristic patterns of alignment between brain regions—as a relational criterion that models must reproduce for genuine brain alignment.
contribution: Shows even top-ranked models fail to capture ROI cross-region alignment patterns, revealing limitations in discriminative power of existing evaluations.

problem: Long-horizon goal-conditioned RL faces challenges from sparse rewards and distant goals; hierarchical methods relying on conventional hindsight relabeling fail to correct subgoal infeasibility.
approach: SSE integrates Frontier Experience Replay to separate unreachable from admissible subgoals, streamlining high-level planning with decoupled exploration and path refinement.
contribution: Consistently outperforms existing goal-conditioned and hierarchical RL methods in efficiency and success rate across long-horizon benchmarks.

problem: Classifier-free guidance produces well-known artifacts (mean overshoot, variance shrinkage) in lower dimensions, but theoretical properties remain incompletely understood.
approach: Connects CFG to high-dimensional diffusion framework showing it reproduces correct target distribution in sufficient dimensions, then proposes nonlinear extension mitigating both artifacts.
contribution: Proves CFG exhibits blessing-of-dimensionality and demonstrates continuous improvements in sample quality, diversity, and consistency via nonlinear extension.
